extensions.scope: Covers the client app (apps/client): the Mail surface, the chrome/shell, Settings, the Screener, the App Switcher, and — as of the completed polish pass (#314-#323, docs/design/polish-pass.md) — Contacts, Calendar, Tasks and Notes' shared control vocabulary, scale, and phone chrome. The repo-facing marks (apps/client/public/{favicon.svg,icon-192.png,icon-512.png,icon-maskable-192.png,icon-maskable-512.png,apple-touch-icon.png,manifest.webmanifest} and docs/brand/{wicket-social-card.png,social-card.source.html}) still carry the postmark mark (src/brand/Mark.tsx) — the one drawn signature glyph that survived the rebuild, not a superseded asset. manifest.webmanifest no longer carries theme_color at all (polish pass ticket 4, R1's Android step 2) — only background_color remains. The sync backend has no UI.

themes.light: Bare :root is the light set (near-white ground), so nothing depends on a media query having matched.
themes.dark: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not(.light) and :root.dark carry the near-black ground. An explicit .light or .dark class always beats the OS.

darkOverrides.note: Accent lifts to a lighter violet (#8b80ff vs #4338ca) in dark rather than staying the same hex, so it still reads as *the* accent against a near-black ground without needing contrast tricks. Source: packages/design-tokens/src/colors.ts.

browserSurfaces.note: index.html's <meta name=theme-color> pair is width- and appearance-aware: --color-surface-strong at >=768px (opaque desktop header), --color-bg below it (the phone header is translucent/blurred over that ground, R1). manifest.webmanifest carries no theme_color at all as of the polish pass (an installed Android WebAPK froze its status bar on the manifest value at install time and never re-read the meta); background_color (#fbfbfc) remains for the cold-load splash.
browserSurfaces.selection: accent ground (color-mix with accent-soft), ink text — src/index.css ::selection
browserSurfaces.scrollbar: thin, thumb var(--color-border) on transparent track

border.note: The one hairline that still exists — dividing rows in bordered-list contexts (Settings, Screener cards); never boxes in a Mail row.

accent.note: The one accent that means primary/current/focus, everywhere. Lifts to #8b80ff in dark.

accent-soft.note: Rank at rest — a selected thread row, the current nav tab, the App Switcher badge. Tint, never inversion.

tile-a.note: Ink pair #3730a3. Deterministic off the correspondent's address (mail/Avatar.tsx), not decorative choice.

tile-e.note: Ink pair #33415c. A closed set of five, not a hue wheel — a scanned list wants variety without noise.

heading.purpose: The open Thread's subject — the loudest text in the app, and the only place 21px appears. text-wrap: balance.

body.purpose: A thread row's subject/sender, message content, running UI text.

secondary.purpose: Meta lines, the reading pane's correspondent line, snippets.

label.purpose: Section labels, group-header names, the Command Palette's section captions. Sentence case, small, quiet — never uppercase, never letterspaced.

machine.purpose: Timestamps, group counts, byte sizes, key caps. Inter tabular figures — Martian Mono retired entirely by the polish pass (decision A).

title.purpose: A pane header — Tasks, Contacts, Notes, Calendar, Settings page headers. Added by the polish pass's R4 pane-title tier so five Apps stop picking their own size.

fonts.delivery: Self-hosted from the app's own origin (Inter Variable only) — a client whose promise is that you own your server has no business fetching fonts from a CDN on cold start.
fonts.note: Martian Mono Variable is retired entirely (polish pass decision A, packages/design-tokens/src/typography.ts). `mono` is now a plain system stack kept for exactly one genuinely code-like run: the compose send-failure banner's verbatim SMTP rejection text. Every machine value and every email address moved to Inter.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system (--shadow-overlay). The Command Palette, the Shortcut Sheet, the composer, popovers, toasts — anything that genuinely floats above the ground. Also the phone Dock's own floating glass pill (polish pass).

shadows.name: header
shadows.purpose: --shadow-header: the global header's separation from the ground. An inset relief, not a drop shadow — the header never floats above anything, it sits at the top of the same ground, so it does not take --shadow-overlay.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: --shadow-card: a page-resident element raised in place rather than floating over everything — the App's own raised card on the Hub (.app-card, >=768px), and the Segmented thumb's own small lift off its track.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Toast/palette entry, grid-column expansion (App Switcher), max-height disclosures.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Icon/badge pop moments — the App Switcher badge, nav icon transform.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Toast/palette entry, disclosure rotation, row hover/selection state.

motion.name: reduced-motion-floor
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce clamps every animation and transition in the app.

motion.name: dur-leave
motion.purpose: A row, card, or group departing after an action (up to 45ms per-row stagger, capped at 8); a bottom Sheet's own rise from the edge (polish pass R5).

motion.name: pane-enter
motion.purpose: Polish pass R5: the phone list-to-detail transition (Mail's split pane, Tasks, Contacts) plays this on mount, replacing a hard display:none swap.

motion.name: segmented-thumb
motion.purpose: Polish pass R5: the Segmented control's sliding current-option thumb, driven by --seg-index/--seg-count.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.note: The one phone breakpoint the whole Client reads (polish pass ticket, @mail/design-tokens#phoneBreakpoint) — collapses two pre-existing numbers (700px and a second shadcn-derived 768px hook) into one. List/detail split, folder rail, Dock vs. desktop header/App Switcher, and theme-color resolution all key off this single value now.

breakpoints.name: compact-header
breakpoints.note: The global header shrinks and the search entry's ⌘K hint text gives way so it doesn't crowd the field.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.note: The split list widens to clear the row-fold breakpoint, so the single-line row layout renders instead of the folded two-line one.

breakpoints.name: row-fold
breakpoints.note: The row folds to a two-line grid. Container, not media.

taper.note: mail/taper.ts: rank expressed as scale, not just position. Row/header heights taper from T1 (Pinned/Today, loudest) to T4 (Older/Undated, quietest); header heights are 26/24/22/20 plus the 26px group-header lead baked in as padding, since a virtualized item can't carry a margin the virtualizer never measured. compact shifts every tier by a fixed delta rather than flattening the taper to one size. Shared contract with VirtualizedThreadList's estimateSize — the ROW_HEIGHT/HEADER_HEIGHT values live once, in code, not duplicated into mail.css.

copy.source: CONTEXT.md is binding for UI copy.

boundaries: The message body is third-party HTML in a sandboxed iframe on its own ground. The design system stops at that boundary and may not restyle what a sender wrote.
Remote images are blocked until a sender is Approved, which is why correspondent marks are circular initial tiles drawn from the address and never fetched.
Density and layout mode are Device Preferences and never sync.
notCanonized: The App Switcher's reserved-App badge ('SOON') carries light tracking (0.03em) at 10px. DESIGN.md records this as a single deliberate, narrowly-scoped exception for a status chip, not as a general allowance to bring tracked caption type back into the system.

Several form-section captions in Calendar, Contacts, and Notes (contact-dialog.css, note-editor.css, etc.) still carry text-transform: uppercase. This predates the polish pass and was outside its R1-R5 scope (which targeted buttons/tabs/filters/scale/hairlines specifically) — DESIGN.md records it under Superseded vocabulary as an unfinished migration, not as a confirmed second voice a new screen should imitate.

The shadcn primitives under src/components/ui/ ship Lucide hairline glyphs consistent with the current icon language; they are installed but adopted by no screen yet, so they are not asserted here as a confirmed pattern.

scale.note: R4 (docs/design/polish-pass.md, packages/design-tokens/src/scale.ts): the whole sizing vocabulary of apps/client CSS outside mail/taper.ts, which predates and defines rank-by-scale rather than consuming this ladder. Before this pass, apps/client CSS used 14 distinct font sizes and 13 distinct paddings.

chrome.note: R1 (polish pass): chrome floats over content on phone rather than framing it. .app-shell declares --chrome-top/--chrome-bottom (both 0px at >=768px); every phone scroller pads itself by these instead of the header/Dock reserving space for themselves. Replaces the pre-pass opaque phone header slab and the reserved-but-empty ground beneath the old dock (the 'gray bar' defect).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one solid-accent action per App (R3): Compose, New contact, New event, New task, New note, Send, Approve. controls.css's .btn-primary. Rendered by both the desktop header's <PrimaryAction> and the phone Dock's trailing tile via apps/primary-action.ts#usePrimaryAction.

components.description: A form control's fill at rest, no border, focus ring in accent. Placeholder-as-label in the composer rather than a caption above the field.

components.description: Signature component: the left header cell. A hub-mark (soft rounded-square tile carrying the postmark and the current App's badge) expands via a grid-template-columns transition into a row of pill tabs, one per App, on open. The current tab takes accent-soft + accent ink and bold weight; a reserved App gets a small 'SOON' caption rather than being hidden.

components.name: The Thread Row
components.description: Signature component: a borderless, rounded row on the page ground. Sender (max 40%, ink-muted), subject (flex, ink-faint), right-aligned tabular time (Inter, not mono), and a Done control revealed on hover/focus/selection rather than inserted. Hover takes color-hover; selection takes accent-soft (a tint, never an inversion). Unread bumps the sender to full ink + weight 600.

One text field, then sectioned rows each carrying a keycap. The active row takes accent-soft. Section captions are the Label tier — sentence case, never uppercase.

narrative.overview:
The Instrument is a near-white (or near-black) ground with exactly one electric accent (#4338ca light / #8b80ff dark) doing every job that matters: primary actions, focus, selection, current-state. Nothing else in the palette is decorative — three ink strengths carry all text, three semantic signals (danger/warn/success) carry all state, and five tinted "tile" pairs give correspondent initials just enough variety to scan without noise. There is no second accent and no per-feature color.

Regions are separated by ground and gap, never by joinery. A list row, a menu item, a settings compartment — none of them sit inside a hairline box or a bordered plate. The one shadow in the system reserved for floating things (--shadow-overlay) covers the Command Palette, popovers, the composer, toasts, and now the phone Dock's own glass pill; a second, shallower token (--shadow-card) covers a page-resident raised element (the App's own card, the Segmented thumb). Rank between things at rest is expressed by a soft accent tint, not by inverting to solid ink and not by a colored badge bolted onto the side of a row.

A completed polish pass (#314-#323, docs/design/polish-pass.md) took the same world further without changing the palette, the accent, ground-and-gap, the taper, the Hub, or the App Switcher: chrome now floats over content on phone instead of framing it (translucent blurred header and Dock, every scroller reserving its own clearance instead); one shared control vocabulary (.btn-primary/.btn-ghost/Segmented/.chip) replaced four Apps' four separate button dialects; one type-and-space scale replaced fourteen ad hoc font sizes and thirteen ad hoc paddings; Martian Mono is retired entirely, with every machine value now set in Inter with tabular figures; and Tasks was brought into Mail's own idiom (its rail, its List/Board Segmented switch, its quick-add ghost row, its ground-and-gap board columns).

This replaces an older system ("Wicket / The Sorting Office" — institutional stock, hairline joinery, struck ink, uppercase letterspaced "plates" for every label) which is fully retired from the Mail surface, the chrome, and the App Switcher. A handful of form-section captions in Calendar, Contacts, and Notes still speak in its retired uppercase voice and are recorded as an unfinished migration outside the polish pass's own scope, not as house style.
keyCharacteristics: One electric accent, everywhere rank or action needs marking; nothing else is decorative.
Ground and gap, not joinery: no hairline box around a control, no plate behind a row.
Rank is a soft accent tint (--color-accent-soft) at rest, --color-hover under the pointer — nothing inverts to solid ink.
Corners come from one ladder: control → row → panel → pill, never an ad hoc radius.
One control vocabulary everywhere: .btn-primary, .btn-ghost, Segmented, .chip — no hairline-bordered button outside Settings.
Chrome floats on phone — translucent, blurred, never a slab; every scroller reserves its own clearance instead.
Type carries rank by size and weight. Labels are sentence case, small, and quiet — never uppercase, never letterspaced.
The document itself never scrolls: the shell owns the viewport, every routed pane scrolls on its own.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: {colors.accent} is the only color that means "this is the primary action or the current thing." A new state does not get a new color; it gets a tint of accent, one of the three semantic signals, or nothing.

rules.name: The Tint-Not-Invert Rule
rules.body: Rank at rest is {colors.accent-soft} with accent ink, never {colors.ink} as a solid ground.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, heading, and caption in the rebuilt system is sentence case. text-transform: uppercase plus 0.10em+ tracking was the old system's signature voice and does not belong here.

rules.name: The One Voice, One Face Rule
rules.body: Exactly one sans face (Inter) for every measured and every written value. A second imported face for machine values was tried and retired (Martian Mono); only a system ui-monospace stack remains, reserved for one genuinely code-like run.

rules.name: The Bounded Pane Rule
rules.body: .app-shell is 100dvh + overflow: hidden; every routed pane is its own height: 100%; min-height: 0 scroller. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Ground-and-Gap Rule
rules.body: Regions separate by background-color change and whitespace, not by a hairline box or a card. Settings is the named exception.

rules.name: The Chrome-Floats Rule
rules.body: On phone, the header and the Dock are translucent, blurred, and sit on top of the scrolling pane, never around it. Every scroller pads itself by --chrome-top/--chrome-bottom instead of the chrome reserving space for itself.

rules.name: The Float vs. Rest vs. Frame Rule
rules.body: If it's part of the frame at rest, it has no shadow. If it's raised in place on the page, it takes --shadow-card. If it floats over the frame, it takes --shadow-overlay.

dos: Do reach for {colors.accent}/{colors.accent-soft} for anything primary or "current." It is the only color that carries that meaning.
Do separate regions by background-color step and whitespace, not by a hairline box; keep the hairline exception to Settings.
Do use the radius ladder (sm → md → row → panel → pill) — never an ad hoc value.
Do use the shared control vocabulary (.btn-primary, .btn-ghost, Segmented, .chip) for any new button, tab strip, or filter.
Do snap every new font size, padding, and control height to the shared space/text/controlHeight ladders — mail/taper.ts is the one named exception.
Do keep every label, caption, and heading in sentence case.
Do set every machine-measured value in Inter with tabular figures — no separate mono face outside the compose SMTP rejection text.
Do give an action reserved whitespace and reveal it on hover/focus/selection rather than inserting it and reflowing neighbors.
Do keep .app-shell at 100dvh + overflow: hidden and give every new routed screen its own height: 100%; min-height: 0 scroller.
Do pad a new phone-visible scroller by --chrome-top/--chrome-bottom — chrome floats, it never reserves space for itself.
Do give a new App exactly one primaryAction and, only if needed, one navControl, resolved through apps/primary-action.ts.
Do use CONTEXT.md's vocabulary verbatim in UI copy: Thread not conversation, Mail Account not mailbox, Screener not quarantine, Verdict as Unscreened/Approved/Blocked.
Do self-host faces from the app's own origin.
donts: Don't invert a selected/current element to solid ink. Rank is a soft tint, never an inversion.
Don't set a label, heading, or caption in uppercase with letterspacing — that is the old system's signature voice.
Don't put a border around a Mail-surface row, panel, toolbar, tab strip, or Sheet edge to separate it from its neighbor.
Don't give a control an ink color at rest. Ghost is the default voice: transparent → hover fill → soft-tint-when-current.
Don't hand-roll a second button/tab/filter shape outside .btn-primary/.btn-ghost/Segmented/.chip.
Don't pick an off-ladder font size, padding, or control height. mail/taper.ts is the one named exception.
Don't animate a list's or Stream's arrival, or stagger cards/rows in.
Don't reach for a second mono/imported face for a machine value — Martian Mono is retired.
Don't let a phone chrome element reserve layout space for itself, and don't let a new phone scroller skip its own --chrome-top/--chrome-bottom padding.
Don't fetch a correspondent's image or a font from a CDN.
Don't restyle a message body — it is third-party HTML in a sandboxed iframe and the design system stops at that boundary.
